fichas.title: Lightning protection systems for roofs and structures
fichas.summary: Illustrated arrangements show lightning protection for steel-framed buildings, metal roofs with timber-clad walls, aluminium roof and wall coverings, chimneys, roof masts, and rooftop metalwork. Conductors connect to earth; metal structures and ventilation ducts on roofs are connected to the lightning protection system. A high-voltage cable roof mast is not directly connected: the illustrated open transmission path has a spark gap.
uses: Connect roof metalwork and rooftop services to the lightning protection system
Provide a spark gap between a roof mast for high-voltage cable and the open transmission path

dimensions.label: Spark gap
dimensions.context: Illustrated open transmission path for a roof mast for high-voltage cable; OCR gives 30 mm.
dimensions.ocr_raw: spark gap of 30 mm

fichas.title: Earthing electrodes
fichas.summary: Earthing systems conduct lightning current quickly and uniformly into electrodes. Surface tapes may be laid as a ring or strip, preferably embedded in foundation concrete. Underground rods are driven into the ground to achieve low ground resistance; a rod driven more than 6 m is described as buried. Star-shaped electrodes consist of tapes projecting outward from a conductor.
uses: Disperse lightning current into the ground

fichas.summary: A reference table gives tape lengths and rod depths for earthing electrodes in six soil categories, arranged by ground-resistance levels of 5, 10, 15, and 30 ohms. The values are reproduced as printed; the table headings identify the soil categories as marshy soil, loam/clay/stable soil, damp sand, damp gravel, dry sand and gravel, and stony ground.

Earthing electrodes
The earthing system has the task of conducting the lightning
current quickly and uniformly into earthing electrodes. These
can be tapes (surface) or rods (underground, sometimes called
'buried') earthing electrodes:
Surface earthing electrodes (earthing tapes) are laid as a ring or
strip, preferably embedded in the foundation concrete. Earthing
tapes consist of galvanised steel strip (30 x 3.5 mm/25 x 4.0 mm)
or round steel (diameter= 10 mm) ~ 4!) - @).
Underground earthing electrodes (rods). These are round or with
an open profile. They are driven, inside tubes, so deep into the
ground without insulation that a low ground resistance is achieved
~ 4!)- @). The level of the ground resistance varies according to
soil type and moisture content ~ $. If earthing electrode rods
are driven more than 6 m into the ground, they are described as
'buried'.
A star-shaped earthing electrode consists of individual tapes
projecting outward in a star shape from a conductor.
